report:
The declared radial singular-obstacle theorem, its measure formula, and its nonclosed product extension withstand independent reconstruction. No concrete mathematical defect was found in these assertions. They establish a specific compact envelope result, but do not establish completion of the unchanged S06 task: conditions for independently prescribed Monge–Ampère equations in arbitrary ordinary or relative types, general compact obstacle sets, and ideal weighted extremals remain open in the supplied argument.

The reference calculation is correct. With a=αT^(α−1), the displayed formulas give 0<A′<1 and A″>0, with A″ bounded. The left tangent intercept tends to −∞; the right intercept tends to zero. The pole is genuinely sublogarithmic and unbounded. Near infinity, R=|Z₀|²/(Σⱼ≥1|Zⱼ|²) is smooth, so the asserted extension of ψ is valid. Both κ and H are positive backgrounds and therefore satisfy the task’s bigness definition with potential zero.

The convex reduction uses the full competitor family correctly. The obstacle supplies local uniform upper bounds, and ψ−‖F‖∞ prevents collapse. Upper regularization preserves the obstacle inequality, including its −∞ value at the pole. Unitary invariance makes the envelope radial without restricting competitors. The radial Hessian calculation gives convexity and nonnegative slope of its total profile. Conversely, the largest convex minorant C has slopes in [0,1], the sandwich bounds force its limiting slopes to be 0 and 1, and local removable-singularity results apply at both projective ends. Thus C−log(1+eˣ) is an admissible global competitor, proving equality and ordinary type retention.

The regularity proof is valid. Chord replacement proves affineness on every free component. At a contact point, C′₋≥g′≥C′₊, together with convexity, forces differentiability and equality with g′. Moving endpoints through free components then proves 0≤C′(b)−C′(a)≤L₂(b−a), including the unbounded-component cases. The left tangent test proves C=A on an actual left interval. At infinity, all alternatives are covered: an attained L=inf(g−x) gives C=x+L on a right tail; otherwise L=0 and the right tangent test gives C=A there. These exact end formulas justify extension of the residual across the pole and hyperplane. The annular Hessian estimate gives the stated global C¹,¹ conclusion, with constants depending on the constructed cutoffs. It provides no uniform C¹,¹ convergence assertion for varying obstacles.

The measure normalization is correct for ddᶜ=i∂∂̄/(2π): the smooth radial density is k!π^(−k)(C′)^(k−1)C″r^(−k), whose polar integral is d(C′ᵏ). Even one-dimensional mollification supplies decreasing smooth convex profiles, so bounded Bedford–Taylor continuity applies on annuli. Consequently the annular mass is C′(b)ᵏ−C′(a)ᵏ. Continuity of C′ excludes radial atoms, the non-pluripolar construction excludes pole mass, and smoothness excludes hyperplane mass. Total mass is therefore one. Free intervals have zero top-degree density. The negative bump example really produces an open zero-density tail; for example k=2, α=1/2, x₀=0 and M=1 work because A(0)<log 2<1. The residual stability bound follows directly by translating competitors and extending their finite residuals continuously.

Both supplied slicing proofs are valid. In the supplementary proof, v+ρ(z)+q(y) has positive complex Hessian because ddᶜρ=κ and ddᶜq≥h₀. Its canonical holomorphic restriction is psh or identically −∞ on every slice. Subtracting q(y₀) and ρ gives exactly κ-psh slices. This establishes the pointwise upper bound for every product competitor; lifting the base envelope establishes equality. The convolution proof in the article also preserves the exact slice bound after its smooth background error tends to zero. No transitive symmetry on Y or generic-slice argument is needed.

At every bounded truncation, the corrected product expansion has only the term with k base factors and m factor factors. Restriction to strict superlevel sets gives the claimed tensor measure and mass binom(k+m,k)V₀. The explicit restricted masses are bounded, so this particular unbounded construction requires no BMP assumption. The Hopf form is positive, scaling invariant and satisfies dh₀=−ds∧ddᶜs≠0. The quotient is S³×S¹; its odd first Betti number excludes a Kähler metric. The product example is consequently a genuine nonclosed non-Kähler fourfold. The stretching-class assertion uses the correct definition and the explicit witness aₜ=ψ−t‖F‖∞. These are actual representative masses, not lower or upper singularity volumes.

The private proposal’s multiplier-ideal aside also checks out: for every t>0, sublogarithmic growth makes exp(−tψ) locally integrable, so I(tψ)=O. Its zero-obstacle ordinary model is indeed zero: for any finite x, a tangent to f(x)=log(1+eˣ) lies below A+c for sufficiently large c; the convex minorant of min(f,A+c) then supplies a type-controlled competitor attaining zero there. Upper regularization erases the isolated pole. This does not identify the article’s obstacle envelope with an ideal envelope.

The indispensable local hypotheses were checked in [Demailly](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf), [Bedford–Taylor](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf), and [Boucksom–Guedj–Lu](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.01090v1). The latter is used only for bounded corrected products. Task passages below record canonical-representative and product conventions; those granted conventions are excluded from the external-premise list.

The literature comparison is accurate for [Ahn’s continuity theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.01885v3), [Ahn’s Hölder theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.01887v3), and [Nguyen’s continuity theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.04171): their stated weights are finite and continuous or Hölder, whereas ψ+F has a genuine pole. Here K=X satisfies capacity density. Thus the demonstrated distinction is the singular weight and retained ordinary type, rather than failure of capacity density. This establishes a narrow residual/envelope result beyond the listed logarithmic and minimal examples; source-hypothesis failure alone does not certify broader novelty or resolve the general weighted programme.

Harmless wording corrections: R should be called a smooth projective function, rather than a coordinate. In the private proposal, the assertion that the asymptotic slopes are 0 and 1 should explicitly refer to C with its sandwich bounds; arbitrary affine minorants need not have those limiting slopes. Neither correction changes the proof. No substantial repair is required for the declared theorems. The unresolved issue is their limited coverage of the original completion criteria.

passages.statement: For a locally uniformly upper-bounded family of plurisubharmonic functions on a complex domain, the upper semicontinuous regularization of its supremum is plurisubharmonic, allowing an identically −∞ component. Demailly, Chapter I, Theorem 5.7.

A distribution on a complex domain with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable plurisubharmonic representative. Standard radial mollifications of a locally integrable plurisubharmonic function are smooth and plurisubharmonic on smaller domains and decrease pointwise to its canonical values as their radii tend to zero. Demailly, Chapter I, Theorems 5.5 and 5.8.

passages.quote: All potentials are genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives, with pole values included.

passages.statement: If f:X→Y is holomorphic between complex manifolds and u is plurisubharmonic on Y, then u∘f is plurisubharmonic on each component of X or identically −∞. Demailly, Chapter I, Theorem 5.11.

A plurisubharmonic function on X\A, where A is a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold X, extends uniquely plurisubharmonically across A if it is locally bounded above near A. Demailly, Chapter I, Theorem 5.24.

For locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on a complex domain, Bedford–Taylor wedge products are closed positive currents and form a symmetric multilinear operator. If each input sequence decreases pointwise to a locally bounded plurisubharmonic limit, its wedge products converge weakly to the wedge product of the limits. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.
passages.quote: where the limit is in the weak topology

passages.statement: On a compact complex manifold, for smooth real (1,1)-forms θ_i and bounded quasi-psh functions u_i, the products of T_i=θ_i+ddᶜu_i defined by expansion into smooth-background factors and bounded Bedford–Taylor factors are independent of the decompositions, symmetric, multilinear, non-pluripolar and local in the plurifine topology. They are positive when every T_i is positive. This bounded-potential assertion requires no bounded mass property. Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Section 2.1, Proposition 2.1.
passages.quote: acting on tuples of quasi-psh functions bounded on K is local in the plurifine topology.

They are positive when every T_i is positive. This bounded-potential assertion requires no bounded mass property. Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Section 2.1, Proposition 2.1.
passages.quote: Extended products are non-pluripolar products with smooth-background corrections.

passages.statement: Every odd Betti number of a compact Kähler manifold is even. Demailly, Chapter VI, equation 8.12 and its consequence.

Using ddᶜ=2i∂∂̄, let (X,ω) be a compact Hermitian manifold and K⊂X a compact non-pluripolar set. Define V_{K,w}=sup{u∈PSH(X,ω):u≤w on K} and V_K=V_{K,0}. If w:X→ℝ is continuous and V_K is continuous, then V_{K,w} is continuous. Ahn, arXiv:2604.01885v3, Theorem 1.4(ii).
passages.quote: If φ:X→ℝ is continuous and V_K is continuous, then V_{K,φ} is continuous.

passages.statement: Using ddᶜ=2i∂∂̄, let (X,ω) be a compact Hermitian manifold and K⊂X a compact non-pluripolar set. Define V_{K,w}=sup{u∈PSH(X,ω):u≤w on K} and V_K=V_{K,0}. If K has uniform density in capacity and both w:X→ℝ and V_K are Hölder continuous, then V_{K,w} is Hölder continuous. Ahn, arXiv:2604.01887v3, Theorem 1.1(ii).
passages.quote: If K has a uniform density in capacity and φ:X→ℝ and V_K are Hölder continuous, then V_{K,φ} is Hölder continuous.

passages.statement: Let (X,ω) be a compact Kähler manifold and K⊂X a compact non-pluripolar set. For the ordinary weighted extremal V_{K,w}=sup{u∈PSH(X,ω):u≤w on K}, a finite continuous weight w:X→ℝ and continuity of V_{K,0} imply continuity of V_{K,w}. Nguyen, Regularity of the Siciak-Zaharjuta extremal function on compact Kähler manifolds, Theorem 1.1(b).
passages.quote: If V_K is continuous, then V_{K,φ} is continuous.
